knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Hands are checked for open cuts before gloves go on, and any cut is covered with a waterproof plaster. Gloves do not replace that check.
Dirty areas are disinfected first, then clean areas, so that germs are not carried from dirty surfaces onto clean ones.
Washroom equipment is used only in the washroom and stored by colour, so that washroom materials never reach clean areas.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied washroom, the learner places the cleaning-in-progress sign, ventilates the room and checks for chemical fumes before starting, observed by the assessor.
The learner checks their hands for cuts, covers a supplied simulated cut with a waterproof plaster, puts on gloves, and states when gloves must be changed.
On a supplied washroom, the learner cleans the dirty areas before the clean areas, using the designated toilet cloth and brush, with the assessor confirming the order.
The learner removes gum from a supplied urinal with a litter picker, restocks the supplied consumables, and reports one planted fault on a fixture.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Washroom clean record completed by the learner
Defect report for the planted fault
stopWorkCriteria: Learner starts work with an uncovered cut
Learner uses washroom equipment outside the washroom
Learner cleans clean areas before dirty areas, and does not correct the order when asked
Learner leaves a product within reach of a customer
Learner forces a blocked toilet or attempts to clear it
